newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng hits all-time high in late trade.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng hits all-time high in late trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index leapt 229 points, or 1.65 percent, to an all-time high of 14,135 in late Wednesday afternoon trade, pushed higher by buying in blue chip banks, brokers said.
Turnover was a heavy HK$15.09 billion.
The market's advance was led by the finance sector, chiefly HSBC Holdings and Hang Seng Bank.
"I am positive about HSBC, but it must be all in the price," said David Williamson, director at Indosuez W.I. Carr.

Williamson attributed the rise in the share to the increase in the weighting of the finance sector in the FTSE 100 to 18 percent from 12 percent and to the upgrading of its credit rating by Standard & Poor's.
"I am now attracted to Hang Seng Bank for the first time in a year," added Williamson. "Investors should lock in some profit on HSBC now and switch to Hang Seng Bank."
HSBC added HK$6.00 to HK$223 and Hang Seng Bank rose HK$1.50 to HK$94.00.
Other blue chip sectors were strong due to upgrades by S&P in the ratings of corporate bonds, brokers said.
China Light and Power jumped HK$1.10 to HK$37.20 and Hongkong Electric HK$0.65 to HK$28.20.
